cells.tense: The repetitions are landing and the person doing them is not bracing against the next one.
cells.act: let one structure collapse that could not hold
cells.ask: Drop a step you keep out of habit, and don't replace it. See whether the practice holds without that step.
cells.core:
The repetitions are landing, and the person doing them isn't bracing against the next one. Attention is the light kept on the work rather than an alarm to answer. That's why the hours sit easily, and why a session can be looked at afterwards without flinching. The quiet is chosen, and it connects rather than isolates.

Put the shape of it down where the shape can be seen, the pattern underneath the sessions, so the direction is visible and not only followed. Then drop a step you keep out of habit, and don't replace it. See whether the practice holds without that step. What comes apart isn't a whole wall; it's one piece of scaffolding you're finally sure held nothing up. The rest of it stands, lighter, and you'd know that sooner by testing it than by carrying it another year.
cells.sheetLine: The work is landing, and the room is quiet because you kept it that way.
cells.verb: practising the same thing until it becomes part of you
cells.place: a clean room where one thing is being worked on

cells.tense: A finished version is already shining in your head, which makes the repetitions you're doing now feel beneath the work.
cells.act: surrender the outcome and keep the act
cells.ask: Before the next session, find the part that matters and begin there. Finish with that part, hands empty, and add nothing to the day.
cells.core:
A finished version is already shining in your head, which makes the repetitions you're doing now feel beneath the work. The refining is real, and it has run past what it was feeding. Solitude that used to be chosen now feels required, and the sessions get shorter as the plans get brighter. The practice is being guarded from the thing that actually sustains it.

There's a minute before starting when the part of the session that matters can be seen. Use it. Begin with that part, finish with it, hands empty, and add nothing to the day. What gets put down is not the practice. It is the pressure on it. Work finished for the day is still work, and the light you keep on it is easier to keep when the grip is looser.

cells.tense: The practice belongs to an earlier stretch of your life, and some part of you hasn't come through that door.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Teach someone something you can already do, and hear what it was worth to them.
cells.core:
The practice belongs to an earlier stretch of life, and some part of you hasn't come through that door. Skill is still there — hands remember plenty — but the daily work has thinned to nearly nothing. Beginning again feels like grabbing at something already taken, so the hand stops before it starts.

A fair trade is the smallest way back. Teach someone something you can already do, and hear what it was worth to them. An hour at most, and no name has to be put on it. One thing goes out and one thing comes back, and once that has happened the ground under the work can settle by itself.
cells.sheetLine: Your hands still know. Let them show someone.

cells.tense: The work is being done by your hands while the name for it stays small, and the name is where the trouble sits.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Answer the next question about your work with the true answer, then do the next bit of it.
cells.core:
The work is being done by your hands while the name for it stays small, and the name is where the trouble sits. People ask what you're working toward and the answer is that a hand is being kept in. They hear the gap; that's why they ask. Something has your attention that a habit doesn't quite explain.

Answer the next question about your work with the true answer, then do the next bit of it. Nothing more needs saying today. The whole road was not on offer anyway — the next step is all that has been visible, and it has carried you every time so far.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is 'practice has felt dangerous' — the record says past experiences made it so, but the events themselves are stated by the person, not by me, so I locate the door and not the room behind it. A reader could reasonably say the discipline never stopped, only went unrecognised, which is the Unacknowledged cell's whole read — if that is wrong, 'show one piece of it once' still costs nothing and still teaches them which pieces they can already do. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'nothing in it points anywhere' — it is neat, and it would land as a verdict on their life, so the ask stands on its own without it. The Balanced ask's moves are solid; Too Much and Too Little are the same capacity read from opposite ends — holding on past the point where the grip is doing anything, and not being able to hold a practice at all.
